transcript: One of my favorite summer theater festivals is officially underway. If you love discovering new musicals and plays before they become the next big thing, then you have to make your way to New York Stage and film. Hamilton Hadestown Galileo all spent some time at New York Stage and film before coming to Broadway. And it's the perfect little escape from New York City. In the summer. It's up in Poughkeepsie. You can go for the weekend. I've done it as a day trip, and every summer they bring together some of the best artists in the world to develop their work. If you’ve followed me for a while, you know that I love to see work in development. There's something so incredibly magical about seeing a show as it's evolving. I got to see the very earliest reading of A wrinkle in time at New York Stage and Film. It was so special. I am really excited about this season. Jake Brasch, who wrote one of my favorite players of this year, the reservoir and one of my favorite musicals Hole is working on Trip Around the sun. I'm so curious about this one, and I'm literally counting down the days for this three day run of Whistle Down the wind, which is an Andrew Lloyd Webber musical I've never seen. It's in collaboration with Deaf West, meaning that it will incorporate ASL, and it's directed by Bill Rouch, who's one of the co-directors of Cats: The Jellicle Ball. so you just know it's going To be something extremely special. For me, this summer is all about getting out of New York City and seeing some theater. And I cannot wait to make my way to New York stage and film.
